NRL Late Mail: Round 25 - Harry good to go; Trell touch and go
Storm captain Harry Grant is a confirmed starter for Thursday night's clash against the Panthers.
Grant has missed two games with a hamstring injury but returns to lead the side in a rematch of the 2024 grand final.
All eyes will be on Latrell Mitchell ahead of the Bunnies' Saturday night clash with as the superstar centre looks to get back on the field before the finals.
Mitchell has missed 11 games as he battles nerve pain in his lower back which has affected his leg and calf, the Bunnies winning six and losing five in his absence.
If Mitchell does get a call-up it could well be off the bench to allow him time to ease back into the fray.

Mitchell trained on Monday and has been running more freely as he builds up to a highly-anticipated return.
The Rabbitohs have lost Adam Elliott to a groin injury, with the veteran expected to miss two to three weeks with a strained adductor.
Meanwhile, Warriors halfback Luke Metcalf will miss the remainder of the regular season after suffering a hamstring injury in last week's win over Brisbane.
The playmaker is set to return in the opening week of the finals.
Metcalf, who returned last week from a four-month lay-off with a hamstring injury, clutched at the back of his right leg after a shot at goal.
He came from the field and Warriors medical staff immediately strapped ice to the back of his leg.
With Te Maire Martin still another week away from returning from a hamstring injury, rookie Luke Hanson will step into the halves for Saturday's clash with the Rabbitohs.
Wests Tigers halfback Adam Doueihi will undergo season-ending surgery that will rule him out of Lebanon's World Cup campaign.
The playmaker dislocated his shoulder in a Round 9 loss to the Sharks and initially delayed surgery in an attempt to kickstart the Tigers finals campaign.
The 28-year-old returned to the field in Round 17 but fresh scans have shown Doueihi requires immediate surgery, with the halfback to go under the knife later this week.
"New scans on Adam's shoulder have showed the time has come to have his reconstruction done. This gives him enough time to be ready for the start of the 2027 season," Wests Tigers head of high performance Peter Moussa said.
Meanwhile, Tigers five-eighth Latu Fainu has suffered a low-grade hamstring injury at training. Fainu was set to return this week after serving a three-game suspension, but will now be sidelined for 1-2 weeks with his latest injury.
In positive news, Sunia Turuva has been named on the six-man bench despite suffering a knee injury last week, while Alex Twal is set to return after missing Round 24 due to illness.
The Roosters will also welcome back James Tedesco from an ankle injury for Sunday's clash against the Tigers at Allianz Stadium.
The Melbourne Storm will welcome back Harry Grant from a hamstring strain for Thursday's clash with the Panthers.
The hooker suffered the injury in the Round 21 loss to the Rabbitohs and is on track to return this week alongside centre Jack Howarth (shoulder) and forward Alec MacDonald (concussion).
Less positive news for Jahrome Hughes , who remains sidelined with a hamstring injury.

There are just 3 regular season rounds remaining and this ensures the intensity in NRL matches is going to be at an all-time high for season 2026. Round 25 begins in Melbourne this week as the Storm host the Panthers . Most would’ve anticipated this to be an early Finals preview, but the fortunes of the host team have abandoned that thought. Still, with quality remaining, a blockbuster contest waits for two capable teams to do battle.
Also, Before You Bet will be providing free previews and betting tips for EVERY game in the 2026 NRL season, so make sure to head over to our NRL Tips regularly to keep up to date with all of our free content.
Storm vs Panthers Predictions & Tips: NRL Round 25 2026
Spirited Storm at their peak
This season has seen a decline in the performance of the Storm but there were positive signs in Round 23 as they dismantled the Sea Eagles in their 42-20 victory as the ‘home’ team in Perth. Going behind early in the first half but fighting back to trail 14-12 at HT, the Storm kicked into another gear in the second half and their opponents were powerless to stop them. In the end, they had 52% possession, a 77% completion rate, ran for 8.2m per carry, and made 446 PCM’s. Their defence was improved too, missing just 23 tackles and resembling teams that have gone before them in previous years.
Knocked off top spot
The Panthers were defeated 12-6 on the road last week by the Roosters, a loss which has also seen them drop to 2nd on the competition ladder. It a tight game which mirrored a Finals intensity, the Panthers were lacking an edge. Expected to struggle with key players absent and other underdone, they must be better should they aim to be at their best. In the end, they had 52% possession but completed at just 73%, made just 7.6m per carry, and created only 3 line breaks. The biggest concern surrounds their defence and the fact that they missed 44 tackles. This area must be improved heading into the Finals.
Stats that matter
- These two sides met in Round 5 where the Panthers prevailed 50-10. They hate traveling south though, winning just 10% (once) of games at this ground (Storm 76%). The Storm have also won 4 of the past 6 games between these two sides.
- In the past 5 games between them, the average margin of victory is 12 points, with 4 games decided by 8 points or less. The total points is low also, averaging just 46ppg.
- It is no surprise that the Panthers are the superior team on both sides of the ball this season. They average 28ppg in attack and concede just 14ppg defensively. The Storm average 24ppg for both attack and defence in 2026.
More to play for
Each side has key inclusions ahead of this game with Grant (Storm) and McLean (Panthers) back from injury; each player has a positive impact on their team’s performance each week. With the Finals approaching, this is a game which could be tricky for the visitors as the Storm are a dangerous team at home; the Panthers also have a horrendous record here. Yet, with more to play for, one would think that the visitors will be too strong. The loss last week might have come at a good time as it refocuses them ahead of the next few weeks. It also shows that they have areas of improvement within their game which must be addressed. Still down on kay players, they will do well to overcome the Storm convincingly.
Nothing would please the home side more than disrupting the momentum of a Finals bound opponent. That being said, a lot would still have to go right for them over 80 minutes to cause an upset. With the Panthers defence remaining strong, they should have what it takes to cover the line in this match and grab a vital victory.

items.body_excerpt:
Andrew Johns expects the Panthers to bring a halt to their two-game losing streak on Thursday night , but only due to one key Storm player’s absence.
Johns is concerned about Ivan Cleary ’s all-conquering team on the eve of September, with Penrith’s buffer atop the ladder evaporating thanks to a run of three losses in their last five games.
Nathan Cleary stares into space in the Panthers dressing room after losing to the Roosters. Nine
The losses have been compounded by significant injury issues, with inspirational captain Isaah Yeo sidelined by a pec injury that might yet end his season and centre Paul Alamoti out with a hand injury. Gun hooker Mitch Kenny, meanwhile, is still to return from a long layoff with a leg injury.
As a result of the rough trot, the Panthers have slid from minor premiers-in-waiting to equal second spot. Two home finals are far from guaranteed and there’s an outside chance they could slip out of the top four by the end of round 27.
It’s with that context in mind that Johns and Brad Fittler expect a tight contest in Melbourne on Thursday night, even against a Storm side out of finals contention in 11th spot and having also lost three of their last five games.
The one factor stopping Johns from tipping a wild upset is Jahrome Hughes , who has had an injury interrupted season and is still unavailable due to a hamstring issue.
Storm coach Craig Bellamy has named Trent Toelau to partner Cameron Munster in the halves on Thursday night.

“Panther just for mine,” Johns told Wide World of Sports’ NRL Tips as he predicted the winner of Thursday night’s clash.
“If Jahrome Hughes was playing for the Storm I’d tip them.”

Johns added that he liked the look of the Storm’s middle forwards better than the Panthers and also preferred the make-up of their bench, which includes Tyran Wishart, Alec MacDonald, Angus Hinchey, Cooper Clarke, Joe Chan and Jack Hetherington.
The return of skipper Harry Grant from a low-grade hamstring strain gives Melbourne its strongest looking team in the past month, but the Panthers will be desperate to arrest their slide and stay in front of the third placed Warriors , who only trail them due to an inferior for and against.

Tui Kamikamica has described his pride at captaining Fiji as announced his immediate retirement on medical grounds after suffering a stroke earlier this year.
Kamikamica, who has not played since Melbourne Storm's Round 4 match against the Cowboys on March 28, had hoped to be able to lead Fiji at Rugby League World Cup 2026.
However, the 32 year-old prop announced his retirement on Thursday.
A respected leader on and off the field, Kamikamica leaves an enduring legacy with Fiji Bati, having captained his country since 2023, with 23 International appearances to his name.
Viliame Kikau hopes to play in a third World Cup with Fiji captain Tui Kamikamica. ©Scott Davis/NRL Photos
Reflecting on his career, Kamikamica said he was proud to finish his playing journey as a Melbourne Storm player and Fijian captain.
“I’m incredibly proud of everything I’ve been able to achieve in the game, representing Storm and captaining my country," Kamikamica said.
“To play for Storm and captain Fiji are memories I’ll cherish forever."
Viliame Kikau and Api Koroisau are the main captaincy contenders for Fiji’s matches against Cook Islands in Newcastle on October 18, Australia in Townsville on October 25 and New Zealand on Gold Coast on October 31.
“He means a lot, he's captained the side and ... the boys love how he leads. He leads with his actions," Kikau said.
"He's one of probably only two or three of us who were born and bred and raised in Fiji and didn’t come to Australia until we were 18 or 19.
“It is obviously unfortunate what happened to him.”
Fiji backs Sunia Turuva and Jahream Bula said the Bati players remain in close contact during the season and were in shock when they learned that Kamikamica had suffered a stroke.

Matty Johns believes Penrith’s “experiment” with Blaize Talagi at five-eighth could be nearing an end as the Panthers prepare for a crucial Thursday night clash against the Storm.
Talagi has once again been named on the extended bench, with no guarantee that the dynamic five-eighth will return to Penrith’s starting line-up for the finals.
Jack Cogger has been solid since filling in for Talagi and is a definite improvement in defence, although Penrith’s uninspiring performance in attack last week had potentially opened the door for coach Ivan Cleary to look for spark and recall Talagi.
That will not be the case and in many ways it would have been an over-reaction given Penrith’s clunky execution last week may have said more about Isaah Yeo’s absence rather than Cogger, while you also have to give plenty of credit to the Roosters’ defence.
“I thought their attack lacked variation when they were attacking the line,” Johns said on ‘Matty and Cronk’.
“There is no doubt he (Nathan Cleary) missed Isaah. He’s got to because they’ve worked as a partnership for just so long, right through the run of success.”
One of the notes Johns had coming out of the game was that Cogger needed to offer Cleary more, which prompted Cooper Cronk to question whether his co-host had changed his mind after initially saying he thought Penrith were better suited with a steady hand at five-eighth ahead of Talagi.
Cronk did admit he “expected a more significant impact” from Talagi when he was injected into the game late for Freddy Lussick, with the 21-year-old throwing an errant pass that was intercepted as Penrith attacked the line.
Johns though questioned if the Panthers are realising, even early in Talagi’s career, that five-eighth may not be the position for him.

That may not happen this year, especially with Casey McLean returning this week which means the Panthers don’t need to find a replacement elsewhere for the injured Paul Alamoti.

Meet the unheralded halves ready to deliver on the big stage
A collection of unheralded playmakers is set to be thrust into the spotlight after a dramatic couple of weeks turned the NRL premiership race on its head.
At first glance it may seem little connects Niwhai Puru, Jayden Sullivan, Jack Cogger and Luke Hanson but a deeper look reveals they have instantly become some of the most important players in the race to the finals.
A mix of steady backups and young guns, the playmakers have been thrust on to the big stage at short notice following injuries to a host of big names, including Braydon Trindall and Luke Metcalf.
Metcalf leaves the field
With their club's finals fate resting in their hands, premiership winning halfback Chad Townsend said it's a golden opportunity to deliver in a big moment.
"First and foremost, it's a great opportunity for all of them," Townsend told NRL.com. "All these guys have been around the squad and played some games here and there. They should be familiar with their role in the team and what's expected of them.
"When you come into these games at the end of the year, you need to narrow your focus into a couple of things. For me in the big games, it was 'kick well and make your tackles'. There's a lot of things as a half that you can get caught up in but for me it was always about how do I narrow my focus and do my job.
"The bigger the games got, the more important it is to home in on the specifics of a simplified role within the footy team. If you do that, the rest of your game flows off it."
Trindall dislocates shoulder while scoring try
While there are similarities among the group, each player finds themselves in a unique position.
Puru is set to replace Braydon Trindall after the Sharks five-eighth dislocated his shoulder in last week's loss to the Raiders.
Trindall hopes to return in time for the finals, but Puru has been tasked with quickly gelling with Nicho Hynes and helping lead Cronulla back into the top four.
An Indigenous All Star, Puru made his NRL debut earlier this year while Hynes was injured and was solid in three appearances. The Penrith junior has impressed in reserve grade, leading the Newtown Jets to the 2024 NSW Cup premiership and has signed with the Perth Bears for their inaugural season.
A premiership winner with the Sharks, Townsend has watched Puru's progress closely throughout the last couple of years and is confident the 24-year-old is ready to step up.
"I really like his kicking game," Townsend said. "That's a big factor of Niwhai that I've enjoyed in his progression. He's continued to be more comfortable in his role the more he's played.
"He's a great runner of the football and he has good control of the game. From where he was 12 months ago to where he is today, he's taken a lot of steps forward.
